# Start work in the right directory

## Problem statement

When `wl ampa start-work` provisions and enters a *fresh* dev container, the
interactive shell is started with an explicit `cd` to the container-local
sandbox path (`/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`) instead of the canonical
`/workdir/project` symlink. Any already-claimed container is re-entered with
`cd /workdir/project`, so the initial entry is inconsistent with re-entry,
confuses the shell prompt (it computes its relative path against
`/workdir/project`), and makes tooling or user commands that assume
`/workdir/project` report the wrong location.

## Users

- **AI agents** launched into a container by `wl ampa start-work`: they expect
  the project to be at `/workdir/project` so scripts, prompts and `wl ampa
  finish-work` resolve consistently.
- **Operators** reviewing/spawning sandboxes: they expect the documented
  `/workdir/project` path to hold regardless of whether the container was just
  created or re-entered.

### Example user stories

- As an AI agent, when I am dropped into a fresh dev container, I want to be in
  `/workdir/project` so that relative paths, the prompt and tooling match every
  other entry point.
- As an operator, when I run `wl ampa start-work <id>` and then `pwd`, I want to
  see `/workdir/project`, not a `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl ampa start-work <work-item-id>` (and its `sw` alias) starts the
  interactive shell in `/workdir/project` for a newly-provisioned container,
  i.e. `pwd` inside the container reports `/workdir/project` (verification:
  manual E2E `wl ampa sw <id>` then `pwd`).
- [ ] Initial entry is consistent with the already-implemented re-entry and
  legacy-container paths, which both `cd /workdir/project` (verification: code
  inspection + assertion that all interactive entry commands reference
  `/workdir/project`).
- [ ] The shell prompt's relative-path segment resolves against
  `/workdir/project` (no leading `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` shown) and
  `/etc/ampa_bashrc` continues to `cd /workdir/project` (verification: manual
  E2E prompt check).
- [ ] An automated regression test asserts that the interactive entry command
  changes into `/workdir/project` and not the container-local
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` path; the test fails against the
  pre-fix code and passes after the fix (verification: `npm test` /
  `node --test` in the ampa project).
- [ ] Behaviour of `wl ampa finish-work` and the `--wait` / re-entry flows is
  unchanged (verification: existing ampa test suite green).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The container project is physically cloned to
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`; `/workdir/project` is a symlink to it
  created by the setup script. The fix must not move the physical clone.
- Must keep the existing pool/template provisioning, `wl sync` and prompt
  behaviour intact.
- Change is confined to the ampa plugin's `startWork` entry command; the ampa
  project is the implementation repository (see open questions).

## Existing state

- The `start-work` implementation moved out of this repository: the
  `skill/install-ampa/` skill and `ampa.mjs` plugin now live in the **ampa**
  repository (`git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/ampa.git`), under
  `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs`. It was removed from SorraAgents in
  commit `ae0d8474` ("install_ampa skill is now in the ampa proejct itself",
  2026-04-10); the `ampa-repo` git submodule pointer was also removed.
- The container setup clones to `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` and
  creates the symlink `/workdir/project` → that path; `/etc/ampa_bashrc` already
  ends with `cd /workdir/project`.
- Re-entry paths (`start-work` on a claimed pool container / legacy
  `ampa-<id>`) use `cd /workdir/project 2>/dev/null; … exec bash --login`.
- The initial interactive entry in `startWork` used
  `cd ${containerProjectRoot} && exec bash --login` (the `/tmp` path).
- **A fix already exists in the ampa repository on `origin/dev`**: commit
  `77856e0` ("fix: use canonical /workdir/project in start-work initial entry
  (SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW)") changes that one line to
  `cd /workdir/project && exec bash --login`. The matching branch is
  `wl-SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW-fix-start-work-directory`. It is **not yet on
  `main`** (normal dev→main release flow) and the local ampa `dev` checkout is
  one commit behind `origin/dev`.
- The fix commit contains **no automated test** and has not updated the manual
  E2E expectations.

## Desired change

Enter a freshly-provisioned dev container in the canonical
`/workdir/project` directory, matching the re-entry paths, and add regression
coverage so the initial-entry path cannot silently diverge again.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs` (ampa repository) — `startWork()`
  initial interactive entry (`distrobox enter … -c 'cd /workdir/project &&
  exec bash --login'`, currently line ~2137 on the fix branch). Also
  `buildContainerSetupScript()` / `/etc/ampa_bashrc` writer if the canonical
  path is factored out.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs` (ampa repository) — add/extend a
  regression test for the entry command.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-start-work-template-escape.mjs` (ampa repository) —
  nearby start-work setup-script assertions if the path is interpolated.
- `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` (ampa repository) — manual E2E
  expectations / documentation of `/workdir/project`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the fix belongs in the ampa repository, since that is where
  `start-work` lives today; the SorraAgents reference in the commit message is
  the originating work-item ID.
- **Risk:** adding an automated test may require refactoring the entry command
  out of `startWork` into a small exported helper (the command is currently
  built inline and spawned directly), otherwise it is only testable via the
  manual E2E script. Mitigation: extract a pure helper (e.g.
  `buildEntryCommand(cName)`) and unit-test it.
- **Risk:** local ampa `dev` is behind `origin/dev`; implementing from the local
  checkout without pulling would recreate/conflict with the existing fix.
  Mitigation: start from the fix branch / `origin/dev`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** while in the entry code it is tempting to refactor the
  pool/template or prompt logic. Any such extra opportunity should be recorded
  as a separate linked work item, not folded into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MLQ8Z6V20C2FPFP** — "start-work Subcommand" (completed) — defines the
  `wl ampa start-work` behaviour this work item corrects.
- **SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O** — "Podman development container for SorraAgents"
  (completed) — parent epic; origin of the `/workdir/project` convention.
- **SA-0MLRGE8T01IHS922** — "When run wl ampa sw do a wl sync" (completed) —
  the `wl sync` behaviour on entry/re-entry, adjacent to this flow.
- **SA-0MLQ8ZT1300Q1MOM** — "list-containers Subcommand" (completed) — related
  container lifecycle command.
- ampa repository commit `77856e0` on `origin/dev` — the existing fix.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The `start-work` code now lives in the ampa repository
  (`SorraTheOrc/ampa`), and the fix for this work item is already committed
  there on `origin/dev` (`77856e0`, referencing SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW), not yet on
  `main`. Should this SorraAgents work item (a) be closed as complete,
  documenting the ampa fix, (b) be migrated/copied to the ampa project's
  worklog (prefix `AM`), or (c) keep additional work in SorraAgents?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the SA implement skill runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree, where the ampa plugin no longer exists, so an
  implementer cannot make the change here without editing another repository.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The ampa fix is a one-line change with no automated
  regression test. Should this work item also add a test asserting the initial
  entry `cd`s to `/workdir/project` (which likely requires extracting the entry
  command into a testable helper), or is manual E2E coverage sufficient?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: no existing test asserts the
  entry command; `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` documents the path but
  is not automated.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** If the fix is accepted as already complete, should the
  SorraAgents work item still record the ampa commit hash/PR and be closed once
  the fix reaches ampa `main`, or closed immediately against `origin/dev`?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the global workflow normally
  closes work items only after the `dev`→`main` release.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MN1M2B810I9YC0U** – Validate Playwright Distrobox compatibility spike (completed)
- **SA-0MPON9P8Z0062VBL** – Child work items created by /plan should start at intake_complete stage (completed)
- **SA-0MKXYO42T0FC6IJR** – Isolated work environments for parallel work (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: container, directory, make, project, right (+3 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — matched: directory, make, project, right, start (+2 more)

# Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts

## Problem statement

The audit SCANNING blocks and docs currently recommend
`scan.py find-workitem <id>` for worklog lookups (wired in by
SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1; guidance refined by SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI).
`scan.py find-workitem` wraps `wl search <id> --json` plus an exact-id
post-filter. Once the wl CLI gains tolerant ID resolution (the ContextHub
feature below), audit agents should use native wl commands for worklog
lookups and `scan.py find-workitem` can be retired.

## Blocked by

- **WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E** — "Add tolerant work-item ID resolution to `wl show`
  (exact-first, unique substring fallback, ambiguity error) for agent tool
  use" — feature request in the **ContextHub** repository
  (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`), created 2026-08-11.

This item MUST NOT start until that feature lands in the installed wl CLI
(the exact-match `wl show` today cannot resolve partial/truncated IDs, which
is why the scan.py wrapper exists). Cross-project dependency — recorded here
as a blocker; not a `wl dep` edge (different worklog DBs).

## Substring-matching guidance (researched — use ONLY the optimal command)

The canonical substring-matching primitive is **`wl list <term> --json`**:
case-insensitive substring match over id/title/description, JSON mode returns
all matches, supports `-n/--number` and filters (see `src/commands/list.ts`
in ContextHub).

`wl search <keywords> --json` is full-text search (FTS, token/prefix-based) —
**not** a substring matcher — and must NOT be presented as one.

Exact / unique-ID resolution: **`wl show <id> --json`** (tolerant once
WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E lands; `scan.py find-workitem <id>` interim).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All SCANNING blocks in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
   (`_PHASE1_SCANNING_BLOCK`, phase2_child, phase2_batch, phase2_deep) direct
   worklog lookups to native wl commands only:
   - substring matching: `wl list <term> --json`
   - exact/unique-ID resolution: `wl show <id> --json`
2. The dual recommendation "`wl search <keywords> --json` or
   `wl list <term> --json` for substring matching" (introduced by
   SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI) is corrected to the single optimal command
   **`wl list <term> --json`** everywhere it appears (audit_runner.py +
   docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md), per the research note above.
3. `scan.py find-workitem` is removed (subcommand, its tests, and references
   in audit-grep-scan-patterns.md) OR deprecated with a clear notice — the
   decision is documented in a comment; `scan.py search-code` and
   `scan.py list-files` remain unchanged.
4. docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/audit-grep-scan-patterns.md
   (incl. the P9 replacement recipe) updated to the native commands.
5. Full project test suite passes (canonical PATH with `~/.local/bin`).
6. Related docs (README, wiki/docs-site entries, code comments, scan.py
   module docstring) updated; no stale `scan.py find-workitem` guidance
   remains.

## Out of scope

- No changes to `scan.py search-code` / `list-files` (bounded code search).
- No changes to the wl CLI itself — tracked in ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E.
- No changes to audit verdict semantics or prompt structure beyond the
  worklog-lookup guidance lines.

## Related work

- SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI — removed stale `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` grep
  guidance from audit prompts (completed, this item's precursor).
- SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1 — wired scan.py guidance into audit prompts (the
  guidance this item replaces).
- SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM / SA-0MSBSOAEM0078LAO — scan hygiene parents.
data.title: Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts (blocked by ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E)

## Goal

Execute the 24-hour experiment: apply the STE100 instruction to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, let it run for 24h, measure metrics, produce comparison report, and revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add the sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md (verified via grep).
2. Record exact wall-clock T0 and commit hash.
3. Run analysis at T0+24h for both [T0-24h, T0) and [T0, T0+24h) windows.
4. Produce comparison report at `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md` with:
   - Metrics table (session count, duration, tokens, cost for both windows)
   - Delta percentages and direction for each metric
   - Notable outliers (output-token-limit errors, extreme sessions)
   - Project and model breakdown
   - One-line interpretation per metric
5. Revert the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change (verified via grep).
6. Record revert commit hash.

## Steps

1. Start parent implementation
2. Implement child tasks first (analysis script + tests)
3. Add STE100 sentence to AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev, record T0
4. Wait 24 hours (or set reminder/automation)
5. Run analysis for baseline window [T0-24h, T0)
6. Run analysis for experiment window [T0, T0+24h)
7. Generate comparison report
8. Revert AGENTS_GLOBAL.md, commit to dev
9. Record results on work item
10. Clean up worktree

## Related

Dependent on: SA-0MU9VSL250092LTY (Build analysis script), SA-0MU9VT5HI001LHKY (Add tests).

## Summary

The 2026-09-26 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident (SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX) was rooted in a repository-override git environment variable exported into agent/test sessions by a launcher **outside** the `skill/` tree. Defence-in-depth now neutralises the *effect* at every in-repo execution path, but the launcher can still export a live-repo `GIT_DIR` (plus `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`) into the **pre-scrub** environment of any process that calls `git` directly. This item investigates that export and removes or scopes it at its source.

## Problem statement

On 2026-09-26 an orphaned audit fan-out inherited `GIT_DIR=<live worktree git dir>`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` and `GIT_PREFIX=` from a launcher outside the `skill/` tree. The in-repo defence-in-depth layers (shared env scrub, release-gate fail-fast, host-wide audit cap) stop that value from reaching test subprocesses, but they remain the only protection: anything spawned before the scrub that calls `git` itself can still be redirected into the live checkout. The exporting process has not been identified and no setter exists inside this repository.

## Users

- **Agent operators / maintainers** running autonomous agents through herdr/Pi: need every freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables.
- **Contributors** sharing the live checkout: need `dev`/`origin/dev` protected even when a launcher is misconfigured.

User stories:

- As an operator, I want a freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables, so a misconfigured launcher can never redirect a git command into the live checkout.
- As a maintainer, I want the process that sets the override identified and fixed at source, so the defence-in-depth scrub is not the only line of protection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The exporting process/script is identified with reproducible, non-destructive evidence (environment of a freshly spawned agent session or a traced process ancestry), and the evidence is recorded in the work item.
- [ ] The export is removed or scoped at source so child processes — panes, `audit_runner`, `run_tests`, and direct `git` calls — never inherit a live-repo `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`.
- [ ] A regression check asserts a freshly launched agent/test session has no repository-override variables before any git-touching step; it fails if such a variable is reintroduced.
- [ ] `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 (residual launcher risk) is updated to name the confirmed source and the fix, or to record why the source could not be confirmed.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Non-destructive investigation.** The live checkout must never be mutated; evidence gathering must use throwaway/fixture repositories and must never point `GIT_DIR` at the live repo.
- **Source, not symptom.** The fix must be at the exporting launcher, not merely another in-repo scrub layer.
- **Cross-repo (Q1 = A).** The likely launcher lives in the ContextHub repository (`packages/herdr`), outside this worklog's repo. This item owns the investigation and evidence; if ContextHub is confirmed as the culprit, the code fix lands in a **linked cross-repo ContextHub work item**, not in SorraAgents.

## Existing state

Defence-in-depth landed under SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX:

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` + `scrub_repository_overrides` / `repository_override_vars_present` / `log_repository_override_scrub`.
- `skill/test_cache.py::_default_runner`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_run_cmd`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_call_pi` pass scrubbed `env=`.
- `run_tests.py --strict-git-env` release-gate fail-fast (invoked by `.githooks/pre-push` for `dev`/`main`).
- `audit_runner.main` host-wide audit cap + `_find_orphaned_audit_processes` / `_warn_on_orphaned_audits`.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 documents the residual external-launcher risk.

Confirmed by search (`rg 'export GIT_|GIT_DIR='` across the repo and tooling): **no setter exists in the SorraAgents repository**. Candidate launchers identified:

- **herdr agent launcher** (ContextHub, external): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` → `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, invoked as `herdr pane run <pane> exec bash run-pi-agent.sh <lease> ...`.
- **herdr downtime worker** (external): `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` forwards `...process.env` to `send-to-pi.sh`, adding only `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` and `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`. It does **not** scrub repository-override vars, so a `GIT_DIR` already present in the herdr process propagates to every spawned pane.
- **git-hook chain** (in repo): `.git/hooks/post-checkout|post-merge|post-rewrite` delegate to `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` → `wl sync`. Git sets `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH` and `GIT_PREFIX` when running hooks, and `implement.py`'s `git_worktree_add` (`git worktree add`) triggers `post-checkout`. The observed `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` + empty `GIT_PREFIX` are the exact git-hook signature, so the poisoned environment was most plausibly inherited from a git-spawned child rather than a static shell `export`.

## Desired change

1. Determine the **origin** of `GIT_DIR` in the launcher environment — which process first set it and why — using non-destructive evidence (Q2 = C): `/proc/<pid>/environ` of pane/agent/audit processes, git `trace2` (`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`) around `git worktree add`/hooks, launcher/hook inspection, followed by **one controlled fresh-session env dump** to prove the end-to-end state.
2. Fix at source: scrub (or refuse to propagate) `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` in the launcher spawn path (e.g. herdr `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`, `run-pi-agent.sh`/`send-to-pi.sh`) and/or stop the git-hook child that leaks the variables. If the culprit is confirmed to be ContextHub/herdr, file the fix as a **linked cross-repo ContextHub work item** (Q1 = A) and note this item's remediation scope.
3. Add a regression check that a fresh agent/test session has no repository-override variables. Ownership follows Q3 = A: the in-repo SorraAgents boundary (launch wrapper / `run_tests.py`) is tested in this repo; the external launcher boundary is tested in a ContextHub test.
4. Update §9.3 with the finding and fix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — update §9.3 with the confirmed source and fix.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — shared override-var list/scrub helper (reuse for any in-repo mitigation or regression check).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — fresh-session regression check and `--strict-git-env` integration.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — orphan/env-evidence hooks for reproducing the audit fan-out condition safely.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_worktree_add` flow that triggers the `post-checkout` hook.
- `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite`, `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — hook chain (`wl sync`) executed by git with `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` set.
- External (ContextHub, cross-repo — Q1 = A, fix routed to a linked ContextHub item): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX** – Test/audit runner leaks GIT_DIR into test subprocesses, corrupting the live checkout and origin/dev (parent incident; completed/in_review).

- **SA-0MUIBWORE001HOLK** – Symlink nested node_modules into implement worktrees (authoritative record for OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT) (completed)

- **Risk:** fixing only the identified launcher leaves other propagation paths. **Mitigation:** scrub at the launcher spawn boundary (one choke point) plus the regression check.
- **Risk (scope creep):** hardening every launcher is broader than this investigation. **Mitigation:** record additional opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this item.
- **Assumption:** the leak is architectural (environment propagation through the launcher) rather than a one-off manual `export`.
- **Assumption:** the `GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` signature indicates a git-spawned child origin; if tracing shows otherwise, the evidence will redirect the fix.

Options: (A) an in-repo SorraAgents test of the launch wrapper/`run_tests.py`, with the external launcher covered by its own ContextHub test; (B) in-repo only; (C) ContextHub only. **Recommended:** A — each repo tests the boundary it owns. — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-08): A.** Source: interactive reply.

All 10 planning/analysis/maintenance skills use placeholder `--ac` values in their final-step `render_report` blocks. Agents therefore pass the work item's feature ACs (unmet pre-implementation), causing the report to show "incomplete" when the skill session actually completed.

SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5 made `render_report()` derive session status from AC verdicts: any unmet → "incomplete". SA-0MUUCNXNG004RG5Z fixed intake by passing concrete process-deliverable ACs. This child fixes the remaining 10 skills.

2. Each final-step block includes a one-line note: "> **Note:** ACs record the *skill session's* own deliverables — not the work item's feature acceptance criteria."
3. No code changes — SKILL.md docs only.
4. Full test suite green (existing tests unaffected by doc-only changes).
5. No new `--ac` lines change the renderer's behaviour; all `--ac` values use the "met" verdict on success.

# PriorityQueue directory lock ignores timeouts — audit slot acquisition can block indefinitely

## Goal (user story)

As an agent running an audit, I want every queue operation in the slot-admission
path to honour its configured timeout, so a peer that holds the queue directory
lock cannot make slot acquisition hang forever.

## Problem statement

`skill/shared/queue.py:282` (`PriorityQueue._acquire_lock`) takes a **blocking**
`fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)` with **no timeout**:

```python
def _acquire_lock(self) -> None:
    lock_path = self._queue_dir / ".lock"
    lock_path.touch(exist_ok=True)
    fd = os.open(str(lock_path), os.O_RDWR)
    fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)      # blocks indefinitely
    self._lock_fd = fd
```

Every public queue operation (`enqueue`, `dequeue`, `peek`, `remove`, `rank`,
`__len__`, `_list_entries`) acquires this lock via `with self._locked()`.
`_acquire_audit_slot()` (audit_runner.py) calls `queue.enqueue`, `queue.rank`,
`queue.peek` and `queue.remove`, so a peer holding `.lock` blocks audit slot
acquisition **without any bound**, defeating the `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`
(default 90 s) and `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (default 0 s, fail-fast) guarantees.

## Evidence

Minimal reproduction — a child process holds the queue lock for 6 s; the parent
calls `peek(timeout=0)`, whose contract is fail-fast:

```
$ python3 /tmp/queue_hang_demo.py
peek(timeout=0) blocked for 5.50s (contract: ~0s)
```

The timeout argument is not consulted because `_acquire_lock()` blocks **before**
any deadline check. Confirmed against `skill/shared/queue.py` at `dev`
(commit 88a404ec).

## Impact

- A process parked inside the critical section (SIGSTOP, deep I/O stall on the
  lock directory, or a long `_prune_stale` sweep) makes every concurrent audit's
  slot acquisition hang indefinitely — the exact "audit slot acquisition hangs
  indefinitely" symptom reported by an agent (mis-attributed to an unreachable
  `localhost:8000` proxy).
- The priority-queue admission contract (bounded wait, then raise
  `TimeoutError` → "concurrency limit reached" verdict) is not honoured against
  lock contention.
- Contrast: the same package's `Semaphore` uses `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` with a
  bounded retry loop, so this is an inconsistency within the shared layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `PriorityQueue` lock acquisition is **bounded**: a peer holding the directory
   lock cannot block `_acquire_lock`/any public op beyond the configured
   timeout.
2. The configured timeout is honoured on the lock-acquisition path:
   `enqueue` raises `TimeoutError` on deadline, and `dequeue`/`peek` return
   `None` on empty/deadline **without** blocking past it.
3. Implementation follows the existing `Semaphore` pattern (non-blocking
   `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` + short retry loop with a monotonic deadline) or an
   equivalent bounded mechanism; no busy-spin without sleep.
4. Re-entrant behaviour within a single `PriorityQueue` instance is preserved
   (nested `_locked()` remains a no-op when already held).
5. A regression test holds the lock from a second process and asserts that a
   `peek(timeout=0)`/`enqueue(timeout=small)` returns/raises within a bounded
   margin rather than blocking for the hold duration.
6. Existing queue tests (skill/shared/tests/) and the full suite pass.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/queue.py` — `_acquire_lock`, `_release_lock`, `_locked`,
  `enqueue`, `dequeue`, `peek`, `remove`, `rank`.
- `skill/shared/tests/` — queue tests.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_acquire_audit_slot` (consumer).

## Constraints

- Cross-process mutual exclusion must be preserved (no lost updates).
- No new required configuration; existing env vars (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`,
  `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH`, `QUEUE_TTL_SECONDS`) keep working.
- flock releases on process exit / crash must remain the stale-lock guarantee.

## Related Work

- discovered-from:SA-0MUV2UBMT008OE2E (audit slot-status endpoint hardcodes
  localhost). The localhost default was a real bug but **not** the cause of the
  reported hang; this item is the actual unbounded-blocking path.
- SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM — priority-queue admission (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`).
- SA-0MSCC02ME009EGCB — prior audit concurrency investigation.
data.title: PriorityQueue directory lock ignores timeouts — audit slot acquisition can block indefinitely

# Ship release must verify in-scope work items are actually closed before reporting success

## Problem

`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` closes each
candidate with `wl close <id> --force --reason "Shipped in v<version>"` and treats a zero
exit code as success. It never re-reads the item to confirm the persisted
`status`/`stage`. The release then prints `All N work item(s) closed successfully.` — even
when some closes did not persist.

This was demonstrated by the ToneForge v0.1.2 release (2026-10-06): the close step
reported **53/53** closed, but only **50** items ended up `completed`/`done`. Three
remained `completed`/`in_review` with no close comment and unchanged `updatedAt`:

| Item | Title |
|---|---|
| TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18 | Add CLI command to register new primitive recipes |
| TF-0MUUELBUD002OEQ8 | Repair main checkout node_modules symlink loop blocking npm/vitest |
| TF-0MMZIW9NQ09MV98G | Convert hard-coded recipes to ToneGraph configs |

Root cause is the `wl` lost-update race fixed/tracked in ContextHub: a concurrent
`wl sync` clobbered the three in-flight closes (see **WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ** under
WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7). The ship skill cannot prevent that race, but it **can** detect it:
right now a lost close is silently reported as a successful release.

## Desired behaviour

After the close step, re-read every attempted candidate and confirm it is terminal
(`status == "completed"` and `stage == "done"`). If any are not:

1. Re-attempt the close once (bounded), then re-verify.
2. Report unclosed items explicitly by id in the release summary — never include them in
   the "closed" count or claim "all closed successfully".
3. Make the discrepancy visible in the step result (e.g. `unclosedCount` /
   `unclosedItems`) so the operator sees the true outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` verifies persisted state (injectable read boundary) for
   each attempted close instead of trusting only the close command's exit code.
2. An item that exits 0 but is not `completed`/`done` is counted as unclosed and listed by
   id; the summary/return value reflects it and does not claim blanket success.
3. A transient lost close is retried at least once before being reported unclosed.
4. Regression tests with injected `getCandidateItemsFn` / `runCloseCommand` /
   verification boundary cover: (a) all closes persist → success; (b) one close is a no-op
   (exit 0, state unchanged) → retried, then reported unclosed; (c) retry re-persists →
   reported closed.
5. `npm run build` and existing ship suites pass.

## Notes

- Root-cause fix is on the `wl` side: WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ (lock `wl close`; child of the
  WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7 lost-update umbrella).
- Related: SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP (close step *falsely refuses* parents with done
  descendants — fixed by SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9 / SA-0MUTYRYEM000EEF7).
- Refiled to ContextHub: SA-0MUX8PYAY0008HFZ (the raw race report) → WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ.

Discovered while implementing SA-0MUMHR0BT007IKAL (discovered-from:SA-0MUMHR0BT007IKAL).

## Problem
Two or more full test-suite runs executing concurrently on the same host deadlock. Observed twice today: two pytest full-suite processes (one per agent worktree) both stalled in hrtimer_nanosleep with <30s CPU after ~30-40 min, and both recovered only when one run was killed (the surviving run resumed immediately).

## Root cause (hypothesis)
TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY defaults to 2. Each outer run_tests.py holds one `test` semaphore slot for the duration of the suite. The suite itself contains tests that invoke nested `run_tests.py` (tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py::TestRunTestsGuardFires) which need another `test` slot. With two outer runs holding both slots, the nested acquires wait indefinitely (TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT inherited from the parent, e.g. 10800s), producing a deadlock. Setting TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 for one run let its nested acquires use the spare slots and avoided the deadlock.

## Secondary flake
tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs calls syncDevWithMain() which runs live `git fetch`/`git push` against the real repo; under concurrent load it hung in ep_poll (socket) and blocked the pre-push full-suite gate. This test is non-hermetic and should be made hermetic (inject/fake the git operations).

## Desired outcome
- Full-suite runs on a shared host must not deadlock (reserve headroom for nested run_tests slots, or make the nested-aware tests use an isolated semaphore dir / PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR).
- tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs must not perform live git fetch/push.

## Evidence
- /tmp/finish-SA-0MUMHR0BT007IKAL.log (slot wait + full-suite gate).
- Kill of one stalled pytest unstuck the other (wchan hrtimer_nanosleep -> poll_schedule_timeout -> R).

# Intake Brief: Allow `implement.py start` to create a clean worktree when main checkout is dirty

## Problem statement

`implement.py start` hard-fails in Step 4 (safety gate) whenever the main
checkout has uncommitted changes outside `.worklog/`. Since `git worktree add
HEAD` creates a worktree from the last commit — leaving dirty files behind —
the safety gate should permit the agent to create a clean worktree and
proceed, provided the agent judges the dirty files are unlikely to affect
the implementation effort.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** that encounter a dirty main checkout (stale
  changes from a previous session, generated artifacts, or unrelated local
  edits).
- **Ralph / orchestration agents** that need deterministic implement runs
  without operator intervention when dirty files are irrelevant.

### Example user stories

- As an agent, I want `implement.py start` to create a clean worktree
  instead of aborting when the main checkout is dirty, so I can proceed
  without operator intervention.
- As an agent, I want to judge dirty-file relevance using the work item's
  description (including the Key Files section), so I don't miss changes
  that could affect my implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `implement.py start` no longer hard-fails on a dirty main checkout.
   Instead, when the agent determines the dirty files are unlikely to
   affect the implementation effort, it proceeds to create a clean
   worktree from `HEAD` (via `git worktree add HEAD`) and logs the
   decision in a work-item comment naming the dirty files left behind.
2. The agent's relevance judgement must consider the work item's
   description — particularly the "Key Files" section — to determine
   whether any dirty file is likely relevant to the implementation
   effort. Dirty files that appear relevant (e.g. they overlap with
   Key Files paths) still abort the start phase with the existing
   operator-ask behaviour.
3. The agent must leave dirty files untouched in the main checkout;
   no stash, revert, or commit of those files is performed.
4. The decision and the dirty-file paths left behind are recorded in
   a comment on the work item for auditability.
5. Automated tests cover:
   a. Dirty checkout with irrelevant files → worktree created, start succeeds.
   b. Dirty checkout with files overlapping Key Files → abort with
      existing operator-ask behaviour.
   c. Clean checkout (no regression — current path unchanged).
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, SKILL.md (safety gate section), and any relevant docs
   entries.

## Constraints

- Must be a **code change** to `implement.py start` (not SKILL.md
  documentation only).
- No stash, revert, or commit of dirty files — files are left untouched.
- Silent operation: no operator prompt; decision is logged to the
  work-item comment.
- Must preserve existing safety-gate behaviour for clean checkouts and
  for cases where dirty files appear relevant.
- The agent's judgement of "unlikely to affect" is guided by the work
  item description (especially the Key Files section) — this is agent
  discretion, not an automated whitelist.

## Existing state

- **SA-0MQP8K03I007DVMM** (completed) — made the safety gate *worktree-aware
  in SKILL.md* (tells agents they can proceed), but `implement.py start` still
  hard-fails with `dirty_worktree=True`.
- `implement.py` Step 4 calls `git_has_dirty_files()` and aborts immediately
  on any non-`.worklog/` dirty path.
- `wl_show()` fetches the work item description including any "Key Files"
  section; the agent can parse this to judge relevance.
- `git worktree add HEAD` creates a clean worktree from the last commit,
  leaving dirty files behind in the main checkout (confirmed by experiment).
- **SA-0MUYEV5AO006V0HK** (open, high) — enable project-local skill
  extensions for dirty-tree path exemptions (different approach; not a
  blocker for this work).
- **SA-0MTYP6T2I00396J7** (open, medium) — `standups/` not gitignored,
  blocking the dirty-tree gate (example of the problem this solves).
- Tests live in `tests/test_implement_dirty_tree_guidance.py` (SKILL.md
  behavioural tests) and `tests/test_implement_start_resume.py` (phase
  start mocks). The `phase_start` function is easily mocked (see test
  `_patch_start` helper).

## Desired change

1. **After Step 4's dirty-file detection but before aborting**, if the
   main checkout is dirty (and not inside a worktree), the agent should:
   a. Fetch the work item description via `wl_show()` (Step 6 is
      *after* this gate, so the agent must fetch it early — or the
      gate logic must be deferred until after Step 6).
   b. Extract the "Key Files" section from the description (if present).
   c. For each dirty file, judge whether it overlaps with any Key Files
      path (simple prefix or basename match).
   d. If **no** dirty file is relevant → proceed: log a comment naming
      the dirty files left behind, continue to Step 5+ (worktree
      creation), and set `report["dirty_worktree"] = False`.
   e. If **any** dirty file is relevant → fall through to the existing
      abort-with-operator-ask behaviour.
2. **Implementation approach** — the gate logic must be deferred until
   Step 6 (after `wl_show()`), because relevance judgement requires the
   work item description. Restructure: Steps 1-5, then Step 6
   (fetch work item), then the safety gate (now aware of Key Files),
   then Step 6.5+ (branch refresh, worktree creation).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_start` function,
  Step 4 safety gate and Step 6 work-item fetch. Needs reordering:
  fetch work item *before* the dirty-file gate, then judge relevance
  of dirty files against the description's Key Files section.
- `tests/test_implement_dirty_tree_guidance.py` — add functional test
  for the dirty-checkout → clean worktree path.
- `tests/test_implement_start_resume.py` — add a mock test for the
  new gate logic (dirty + relevant vs. dirty + irrelevant).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — update the safety gate section to
  reflect the new code behaviour (agents no longer need to manually
  create worktrees; the script does it).

## Related work

- **SA-0MQP8K03I007DVMM** — Implement skill safety gate should account
  for git worktrees (completed; SKILL.md was updated, code was not).
- **SA-0MUYEV5AO006V0HK** — Enable project-local skill extensions for
  dirty-tree exemptions (open; different approach).
- **SA-0MTYP6T2I00396J7** — standups/ not gitignored, blocking the
  dirty-tree gate (example of the problem this solves).
- **SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2** — Enforce git worktree usage for all
  implementation work (completed; established worktree-first workflow).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — safety gate section to update.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — main file to change.

## Risks & assumptions

- **False negatives**: Agent might judge a dirty file as irrelevant when
  it is relevant (e.g. a helper module imported from an untracked file
  not listed in Key Files). Mitigation: the agent should be conservative
  — if uncertain, abort with operator-ask.
- **Scope creep**: The fix could expand into a broader dirty-tree
  exemption system (e.g. a `.pi/skills_extensions/implement/`
  configuration). Mitigation: keep this change to agent-discretion
  only; record broader improvements as linked work items.
- **Assumptions**: `wl_show()` is called before the safety gate in the
  new flow, so the work item description is available for Key Files
  parsing. The Key Files section format is consistent across work
  items (a Markdown list with file paths).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Code change or documentation only?" — Answer (operator): Code change to `implement.py start`.
- Q: "How should the agent judge relevance?" — Answer (operator): Agent discretion, guided by the work item's description (especially the Key Files section). The agent evaluates each dirty file and proceeds only if none seem relevant.
- Q: "Operator notification?" — Answer (operator): Silent. The agent logs the decision and the dirty files left behind in a work-item comment.

# Intake Brief: ship — `run-release.js --help` runs post-release steps against a stale tag

## Goal (user story)

As a release operator, when I pass an unsupported flag (e.g. `--help`) to the
ship release wrapper, I want the wrapper to **fail fast with usage** and make
**no** git, worklog, notification, or close-side-effects, so that a mistaken or
exploratory invocation can never close release-ready work items without a real
`dev` → `main` merge.

## Problem statement

`node $(skill_path ship)/scripts/run-release.js --help` did not print wrapper
help. Instead it ran the entire post-release tail of the wrapper:

- it forwarded `--help` to the canonical merge script
  (`scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`), which printed its own usage and
  exited `0` **without merging**;
- Step 8 then read the *latest existing* tag via
  `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` (returning the already-shipped `v0.1.18`);
- `verifyReleaseMerge('0.1.18')` **passed** because that tag already exists on
  `origin/main` and is an ancestor of it;
- the wrapper therefore sent a Discord release notification and ran
  `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease('0.1.18')`.

Observed on 2026-10-09 (project `tce-main-street`, dev 72 commits ahead of
main, no merge performed): **98 work items were spuriously closed** (152 close
comments — 150 `Closed with reason: Shipped in v0.1.18` plus 2 cascade
comments). The worklog was subsequently restored to its exact pre-incident
state (0 item-state diffs, 0 extra/missing comments) from the full worklog
snapshot `588ff39` + delta `e7357f3`.

## Root causes

1. `releaseScriptForwardArgs()` strips only documented wrapper-only flags
   (`--skip-checks`, `--refresh-audits`, `--skip-audit-remediation`) and
   forwards everything else — including `--help`/`-h`/unknown flags — to the
   merge script.
2. A merge-script exit `0` is treated as a successful release regardless of
   whether a new tag/merge was produced.
3. Merge verification keys off `git describe` (the newest *reachable* tag),
   which can be an old, already-released tag, so it does not prove *this* run
   produced a release.

## Acceptance criteria

- `run-release.js --help` and `run-release.js -h` print wrapper usage and exit without invoking any gate, merge script, `wl`, git-mutation, Discord notification, or close command.
- An unrecognised flag causes a non-zero exit with usage text; unknown flags are never silently forwarded to the merge script.
- Post-release steps (Discord notification, `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`) run only when the released version tag was **newly created by this run** (did not exist before the run) and its commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`.
- Regression test: with `--help` and with a bogus flag, asserts zero side effects (no `wl close`, no `sendReleaseNotification`, no merge subprocess).
- A merge-script invocation that exits `0` without producing a new tag is detected and does not run post-release steps.

## Evidence

- Incident window comments: 2026-10-09T07:36:05–07:36:10Z, author `worklog`
  (`Closed with reason: Shipped in v0.1.18`) and author `ship` (cascade).
- Pre-incident snapshot ref: `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data`
  full `588ff39` + delta `e7357f3` (2026-10-09T07:34Z).
- `origin/main` stayed at `eebde87`; no `release/*` branch or new tag created.

## Constraints

- Must not weaken merge verification; the fix must be strictly more
  conservative.
- Preserve the existing documented flag set and behaviour for the normal
  no-arg release path.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MRHQC1SJ007WLBW** – Add critical-priority item gating to ship skill release process (completed)
- **SA-0MQJIL0KK003BO55** – Implement: ready_to_merge stage in workflow (completed)
- **SA-0MSGN5OJ4002OZKY** – Cache full test-suite results for reuse across ship/audit/implement workflows (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, already, ancestor, arg, audit (+145 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: acceptance, already, ancestor, arg, asserts (+140 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: abbrev, ahead, already, ancestor, arg (+124 more)
data.title: ship: run-release.js --help runs post-release steps and closes items against a stale tag

# Add a tests-deleted-vs-added health metric and actively prune tests that no longer map to behaviour

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the test-churn analysis to report test deletions as well as additions, and to support pruning tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, so the suite does not grow without bound.

## Background

The ContextHub analysis found the suite grows roughly 8:1 (82,381 added vs 9,968 deleted lines in modified test files) and is ~2.17x the production source by code lines. The current tool's `--diff-filter=ADMR` also hides whole-file test deletions entirely, so pruning is invisible to the metrics.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The analysis reports, per project and per test area: tests added, tests deleted, tests modified, and net growth, in the human report and JSON.
2. Whole-file test deletions are counted (diff filter includes D; rename detection applied so moves are not miscounted as deletions).
3. A documented review workflow describes how to identify and remove tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, referencing `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.
4. The growth metric is trended over time (per quarter or per release) so regressions are visible.
5. Tests cover the added/deleted accounting, including files deleted and re-added.
6. The metric is exposed by the reproducible skill (see the migration epic) rather than as a standalone script.

## Depends on

The reproducible test-churn skill migration epic (metric implemented there).
data.title: Add tests-deleted-vs-added health metric and actively prune tests that no longer map to behaviour

# Run mutation testing on top-churn modules to measure real test value

## Goal

As a producer, I want an empirical measure of whether the largest test suites actually detect faults, so conclusions about TDD return on investment rest on evidence rather than churn proxies.

## Background

Churn and line-count metrics cannot tell us whether tests earn their keep. The top-churn / largest suites identified by the ContextHub analysis (e.g. `downtime-worker.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `sync.test.ts`, `database.test.ts`) are mock-heavy; mutation testing directly measures whether they detect injected faults. This is the recommended follow-up before firm TDD-ROI conclusions in WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A mutation-testing tool is selected and documented (e.g. Stryker for TypeScript, mutmut for Python), with rationale and licensing.
2. The tool runs against at least the top three churn modules of a target project and reports a mutation score per module and overall.
3. Results are compared with test size/mock density to test the hypothesis that high-volume mock-heavy suites have lower mutation scores.
4. Findings are written up and appended to the TDD-value assessment, with explicit caveats (sampling, runtime cost, equivalent mutants).
5. The campaign is reproducible (pinned tool version, documented command) and does not regress the project test suite.
6. Runtime cost is measured and bounded so the campaign can be run periodically.

## Depends on

The reproducible test-churn skill migration epic (provides top-churn input).
data.title: Run mutation testing on top-churn modules to measure real test value

# Create scheduled tasks to run the test-churn skill on all projects

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the test-churn / test-health skill to run automatically on a schedule across all local projects, so test-suite growth and rewrite trends are monitored continuously without manual effort.

## Background

SorraAgents already supports scheduled prompts via `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (entries with `id`, `prompt`, `intervalDays`, optional `time`, `lastTriggeredAt`), used by e.g. `/skill:refactor` and `/skill:standup`. The new test-churn skill should be registered the same way for each project.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A scheduled entry is added for the test-churn/test-health skill in `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (or the project-appropriate scheduled-prompts file) using the existing schema.
2. The schedule runs for every managed project, either via per-project entries or a single command that iterates configured project roots.
3. Output is written to a predictable location (e.g. `reports/test-churn/<date>.md`) and is idempotent (a re-run does not create duplicates).
4. Failures are surfaced (non-zero exit / logged) and do not silently pass.
5. The schedule interval is configurable and documented; the default is documented with a rationale.
6. Tests cover the scheduled-entry wiring or the iteration/adapter used to fan out across projects.
7. The setup is documented in the skill's SKILL.md and in the SorraAgents README/docs.

## Depends on

The reproducible test-churn skill migration epic (the skill must exist first).
data.title: Create scheduled tasks to run the test-churn skill on all projects
